doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Cage on songs, cane work, records and family
title: The song 'You Don't Know My Mind'
summary: The interviewer asks about the first song Cage played; Cage names it 'You Don't Know My Mind' and says he played it all the time.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you want to ask some questions? I'm running out of questions, you know. You are. Well. Now did you, I don't know. I don't have any questions. Really. You know that first song you played when we came here? Yeah. Da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da-da. Remember that?
Yeah. That's You Don't Know My Mind.
Oh yeah. I heard a record of that by a guy named Henry Sims I think. Did you ever hear of him?
No, I didn't know where you are then, but I used to play that all the time.
Yeah, I guess it went around sort of.
You know, when they see me laughing, I'm laughing, and they keep from crying.
